newsitem.title: UK: Four bomb plot suspects appear in British court.
newsitem.headline: Four bomb plot suspects appear in British court.

text.p: Four men appeared in a British court on Monday charged with plotting bomb attacks following police raids last week in which one suspect was shot dead.

The four were arrested after police discovered 10 tonnes of explosives in raids on houses in London that dealt a severe blow to the Irish Republican Army in its guerrilla war to end British rule of Northern Ireland.
The men appeared at the high security Belmarsh court in east London charged with conspiring to cause explosions and possession of explosives. They were remanded in custody until October 9.

Their appearance coincided with the resumption of multi-party peace talks which have been plagued with wrangling between majority Protestant pro-British parties and minority Catholic Irish politicians.
Sinn Fein, the IRA's politial wing, is barred from the talks because the guerrilla group has refused to call off hostilities.
Police said they believed their raids had foiled IRA truck bombs and attacks on high profile public figures just hours before they were due to take place.
But they were criticised by Sinn Fein for killing a fifth suspect, Diarmuid O'Neill, who was apparently unarmed, during the raids.

The discovery of the explosives squashed hopes that the IRA might be considering renewing a 17-month ceasefire it abandoned on February 9 this year accusing the British government of instransigence in the peace talks.
